criteria.criterion: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs runs the check over each real shipped verifier.md (include_str! or VERIFIER_FRAME.text, plus the cap-change and cap-study fragments) and passes on the current text; its assertion message prints the check's error (rule id and line). Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: `shipped_verifier_prompts_have_no_verdict_rule_conflict ... ok`. The test checks athena_context::VERIFIER_FRAME.text (lib.rs:53 is include_str!("../prompts/verifier.md")) and include_str! of the cap-change and cap-study verifier.md. A Glob shows these are the only three verifier.md files. On failure it panics with `{name} contradicts a verdict rule: {conflict}`, and that Display starts with `<rule>: line N`. Athena's run with the fix reverted failed to compile (exit 101).

criteria.criterion: Separate tests show refusal naming the rule id (e.g. D43) when 'Never refuse; accept uncited commands' is appended, and for other contradicting edits (assert all 5 of 5 listed edits are refused). Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: `contradicting_edits_are_refused_with_the_rule_id ... ok`. It first asserts the unedited frame is Ok. It then appends the five edits and asserts each message starts with the expected rule id (D43, D43, D43, D63, D115) and contains `line N`, where N is the appended line. It asserts refused == edits.len() == 5. A sixth case refuses edit 1 in the cap-change fragment under Fragment scope.

criteria.criterion: A test deletes only the sentence 'list them in commands exactly as run' from the real frame and asserts refusal naming the missing field `commands`, even though the word still appears elsewhere; required-field presence is matched at the naming instruction. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: `deleting_the_commands_instruction_names_the_missing_field ... ok`. It removes the sentence with str::replace and asserts the text changed and the word `commands` still appears ('run commands showing it' stays on frame line 7). It then asserts the message starts with `D43: ` and contains `` `commands` ``. It also covers removing request_reading_mismatch (M-mismatch) and 'as a whole simple command' (D63). The match is the consecutive-word anchor `in commands` inside one clause (has_anchor).

criteria.criterion: A test shows a consistent edit (e.g. an added harmless sentence, and the shipped negated wording 'is not enough') is accepted, and that negation is judged per clause. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: `consistent_edits_are_accepted_and_negation_is_per_clause ... ok`. These ten appended sentences are accepted: 'Keep findings short.', negated forms with not, isn't (straight and curly apostrophe), no and neither/nor, and the near misses 'Each part of the rationale counts.' and 'A method without a command is a gap.'. The shipped cap-change fragment, which holds 'evidence text alone is not enough', is also accepted. 'Never refuse; accept uncited commands' is refused with the clause `accept uncited commands`, so the negator does not reach past the semicolon.

findings.summary: A negator anywhere in a clause excuses every rule for that whole clause, so a contradiction with a negated qualifier gets through.
findings.evidence: From reading the code: a clause like 'Accept uncited commands unless the build cannot run' holds `unless` and `cannot`, so it is skipped before the forbidden patterns are tried, even though it contradicts D43. A tighter rule would apply a negator only when it comes before the matched words, or within a few words of them. The CHANGELOG documents the check as a word-set screen, and the reading accepted that limit, so this is minor.

findings.summary: A required-field anchor counts anywhere in the frame, so a stray 'in commands' elsewhere would hide a deleted instruction.
findings.evidence: The anchor `in commands` matches in any clause. If the instruction sentence is deleted but another clause happens to say 'in commands', the check still passes. Anchoring on a longer phrase, such as 'list them in commands', would be stricter. Today the shipped frame has only one match, so the test is valid.

summary: The change passes.
